![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13950745/assets/c8d69cebc1c7388bb9bc8ac73152a9b2941156188917ee6b680f6758a3d777de.png)

Calculate the $x$-coordinates of the points where the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{9} - \dfrac{y^2}{25}=1$ intersects the line $y = x.$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $y=x,$ we first replace $y$ with $x$ in the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{9}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{25} & =1 \\ \frac{16{x}^{2}}{225} & =1 \\ {x}^{2} & =\frac{225}{16} \\ x & =\pm \frac{15}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The hyperbola $6{x}^{2}-8{y}^{2}=24$ intersects the line $x=2$ at

$($
{{field-1}}, 
{{field-2}} $).$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the points where the hyperbola intersects the line $x=2,$ we substitute $x=2$ into the equation of the hyperbola and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}-8{y}^{2} & =24 \\ 6(2)^{2}-8{y}^{2} & =24 \\ 24-8{y}^{2} & =24 \\ -{y}^{2} & =0 \\ y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hyperbola intersects the vertical line $x=2$  at $(2,0).$
